precepts.text: The two trumpets of silver were made for the calling of the assembly and for the journeys of the camps.
precepts.point: That trumpet in the mount was not blown by Moses, for Moses was down among the people sanctifying them; the trumpet came from heaven.

note.label: Exodus 19: The Covenant at Mount Sinai

precepts.why:
At the mount, “when the trumpet soundeth long, they shall come up to the mount.” The trumpets are what gather the people: “Make thee two trumpets of silver; of a whole piece shalt thou make them: that thou mayest use them for the calling of the assembly, and for the journeying of the camps.”

The two trumpets of silver were made for the calling of the assembly and for the journeys of the camps, and trumpets still gather the congregation at the new moons and at the start of classes.

But the trumpet in the mount was not blown by Moses. Moses was down among the people sanctifying them. That trumpet came from heaven.

precepts.text: On the east side toward the rising of the sun pitch the standard of the camp of Judah, with Issachar and Zebulun beside him.
precepts.point: When the alarm is blown the second time, the camps that lie on the south side take their journey: that was Reuben, Simeon, and Gad. The alarm for the journeys was short bursts.

note.label: Numbers 10: The Silver Trumpets and the Order of the Journeys

precepts.why:
“When ye blow an alarm, then the camps that lie on the east parts shall go forward.” Numbers 2 shows who lay on the east parts. “And on the east side toward the rising of the sun shall they of the standard of the camp of Judah pitch throughout their armies: and Nahshon the son of Amminadab shall be captain of the children of Judah.” Next to him pitched “the tribe of Issachar: and Nethaneel the son of Zuar shall be captain”, and “Then the tribe of Zebulun: and Eliab the son of Helon shall be captain of the children of Zebulun.”

So the camps that went forward first at the alarm were Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun, under the standard of the camp of Judah. The alarm for the journeys was short bursts, and at the first alarm the east side, the camp of Judah, took the lead.

precepts.text: On the south side is the standard of the camp of Reuben, with Simeon and Gad beside him.
precepts.point: When the alarm is blown the second time, the camps that lie on the south side take their journey: that was Reuben, Simeon, and Gad. The alarm for the journeys was short bursts.

note.label: Numbers 10: The Silver Trumpets and the Order of the Journeys

precepts.why:
“When ye blow an alarm the second time, then the camps that lie on the south side shall take their journey.” Numbers 2 names the south side. “On the south side shall be the standard of the camp of Reuben according to their armies: and the captain of the children of Reuben shall be Elizur the son of Shedeur.” Those which pitched by him were “the tribe of Simeon: and the captain of the children of Simeon shall be Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai”, and “Then the tribe of Gad: and the captain of the sons of Gad shall be Eliasaph the son of Reuel.”

So at the second alarm Reuben, Simeon, and Gad took their journey, under the standard of the camp of Reuben. Each alarm of short bursts moved the next side of the camp in order: “they shall blow an alarm for their journeys.”

precepts.text: For if the trumpet give an uncertain sound, who shall prepare himself to the battle?
precepts.point: The sons of Aaron the priests blew the trumpets, an ordinance for ever throughout your generations. In war in your land against the enemy that oppresseth you, blow an alarm, and ye shall be remembered before the Lord your God and saved from your enemies. As Israel marched through the wilderness against the nations, the Most High remembered them and destroyed the enemy, as long as they were keeping the commandments.

note.label: Numbers 10: The Silver Trumpets and the Order of the Journeys

precepts.why:
“But when the congregation is to be gathered together, ye shall blow, but ye shall not sound an alarm.” The gathering was a longer sound, a different tone from the short alarm bursts of the journeys, letting everybody know this is the gathering.

“For if the trumpet give an uncertain sound, who shall prepare himself to the battle?” The sound had to be certain. If the priests blew an uncertain sound, people would sit still when it was time to go to war, or try to gather when it was time to go to war.

That is why the sons of Aaron the priests blew the trumpets as “an ordinance for ever throughout your generations”, and why in war “against the enemy that oppresseth you” they were to “blow an alarm with the trumpets; and ye shall be remembered before the Lord your God, and ye shall be saved from your enemies.” As Israel marched through the wilderness against the nations, the Most High remembered them and destroyed the enemy, as long as they were keeping the commandments.

precepts.text: The moon declares the times and seasons and is the sign of feasts; her cycle marks the beginnings of the months.
precepts.point: The beginnings of the months are marked by the moon: the Most High made the moon to serve in her season for a declaration of times, a light that decreaseth in her perfection and then increaseth in her changing, and the month is called after her name. When the light is full again, that is the new moon.

note.label: Numbers 10: The Silver Trumpets and the Order of the Journeys

precepts.why:
The trumpets were blown “in the day of your gladness, and in your solemn days, and in the beginnings of your months”, over the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, “for a memorial before your God.” The beginnings of the months are marked by the moon.

“He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world. From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection. The month is called after her name, increasing wonderfully in her changing.” The moon declares the times and seasons and is the sign of the feasts; her cycle marks the beginnings of the months. Her light decreases in her perfection and then increases in her changing, and when the light is full again, that is the new moon.

The feast days must be a glad moment even to this day. Coming to congregate with your brothers and sisters grudgingly is one of the reasons Israel went into captivity: we were not glad to do what the Most High said.

precepts.text: If thy children will keep my covenant and my testimony, their children shall also sit upon thy throne for evermore.
precepts.point: The testimony is the commandments of the Most High. If the children keep his covenant and his testimony, their children shall sit upon the throne for evermore; and it is his testimony, not our own testimony, that is righteous and very faithful and that changes the people.

note.label: Numbers 10: The Silver Trumpets and the Order of the Journeys

precepts.why:
The cloud was taken up “from off the tabernacle of the testimony.” The testimony is the commandments of the Most High.

“If thy children will keep my covenant and my testimony that I shall teach them, their children shall also sit upon thy throne for evermore.” The testimony is what He teaches, and keeping His covenant and His testimony is what puts the children on the throne for evermore.

So the tabernacle the cloud rested on was the tabernacle of His commandments, and Israel took their journeys out of Sinai following the God whose testimony they were to keep.

precepts.text: Thy testimonies that thou hast commanded are righteous and very faithful.
precepts.point: The testimony is the commandments of the Most High. If the children keep his covenant and his testimony, their children shall sit upon the throne for evermore; and it is his testimony, not our own testimony, that is righteous and very faithful and that changes the people.

note.label: Numbers 10: The Silver Trumpets and the Order of the Journeys

precepts.why:
The tabernacle of the testimony is the tabernacle of the commandments of the Most High. “Thy testimonies that thou hast commanded are righteous and very faithful.”

It is His testimony, not our own testimony, that is righteous and very faithful. What He commanded is what changes the people, and that is what the cloud rested over as Israel journeyed from the wilderness of Sinai to the wilderness of Paran.

precepts.text: The testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple; it is the laws of the Most High that must be taught, for his laws change the people, not our testimony.
precepts.point: The testimony is the commandments of the Most High. If the children keep his covenant and his testimony, their children shall sit upon the throne for evermore; and it is his testimony, not our own testimony, that is righteous and very faithful and that changes the people.

note.label: Numbers 10: The Silver Trumpets and the Order of the Journeys

precepts.why:
“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” The testimony of the tabernacle of the testimony is the law of the Most High, and it is sure.

It is the laws of the Most High that must be taught, for His laws change the people, not our testimony. The law converts the soul and makes wise the simple. Our own testimony does not do that; His does.

That is what the children of Israel carried out of the wilderness of Sinai when the cloud was taken up: the testimony of the Lord, righteous, very faithful, and sure.

precepts.text: The stranger that dwelleth with you shall be unto you as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself; that is why Moses offered Hobab the same goodness.
precepts.point: What goodness the Lord shall do unto us, the same will we do unto thee: Moses treated him as one born among Israel, as a brother; whatever we get, you are going to get. That is the law of the stranger, and it is why Moses dealt so with his kinsman.

note.label: Numbers 10: The Silver Trumpets and the Order of the Journeys

precepts.why:
Moses said to Hobab, his kinsman by marriage, “what goodness the Lord shall do unto us, the same will we do unto thee.” Whatever we get, you are going to get. Moses treated him as one born among Israel, as a brother, and this is the law behind it.

“But the stranger that dwelleth with you shall be unto you as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself; for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God.” That is the law of the stranger, and it is why Moses dealt so with his kinsman.

Hobab knew the land and how they ought to encamp in the wilderness, so Moses asked him to stay and be to them “instead of eyes”; and because of the law of the stranger, the goodness the Lord did unto Israel would be done unto Hobab too.

precepts.text: Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered; as smoke is driven away, as wax melteth before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.
precepts.point: The Most High was fighting Israel's battles and winning the wars. It was not because Israel was a great nation of itself that the other nations were defeated; it was because God was with them, the God that brought them out of Egypt and multiplied them into a great nation.

note.label: Numbers 10: The Silver Trumpets and the Order of the Journeys

precepts.why:
Every time the ark set forward Moses said, “Rise up, Lord, and let thine enemies be scattered; and let them that hate thee flee before thee.” David sang the same words: “Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered: let them also that hate him flee before him.”

David goes on: “As smoke is driven away, so drive them away: as wax melteth before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.” The enemies were scattered at the presence of God, not at the presence of Israel.

The Most High was fighting Israel's battles and winning the wars. It was not because Israel was a great nation of itself that the other nations were defeated; it was because God was with them, the God that brought them out of Egypt and multiplied them into a great nation. The ark went before them to search out a resting place, the cloud of the Lord was upon them by day, and when the ark rested Moses said, “Return, O Lord, unto the many thousands of Israel.”

precepts.text: If ye go to war against the enemy that oppresseth you, blow an alarm with the trumpets, and ye shall be remembered before the Lord and saved from your enemies.
precepts.point: This is the spirit behind the men of Israel rehearsing the righteous acts with trumpets and shofars today, at the camps and at the new moons; it is spiritual and an act of faith.

note.label: Joshua 6: The Fall of Jericho and the Faith of Rahab

precepts.why:
The battle plan came from the Lord: seven priests bearing seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark, and at the long blast the great shout, and the wall falls down flat. The trumpets were commanded for war: “And if ye go to war in your land against the enemy that oppresseth you, then ye shall blow an alarm with the trumpets; and ye shall be remembered before the Lord your God, and ye shall be saved from your enemies.”

The blowing of the trumpets activates the armies of the Lord, the angels, to help in battle. Remember Elisha's servant: when his eyes were opened he saw the host of angels that were there warring and protecting Israel. Blow the alarm, be remembered before the Lord, and be saved from your enemies; that is what happened at Jericho.

This is the spirit behind the men of Israel rehearsing the righteous acts with trumpets and shofars today, at the camps and at the new moons; it is spiritual and an act of faith.

precepts.text: If ye go to war in your land against the enemy that oppresseth you, then ye shall blow an alarm with the trumpets, and ye shall be remembered before the Lord your God, and saved from your enemies. This is the history behind the shofars we blow; those trumpets are not just for looks and thumbnails, there is a deep meaning behind them going into the memorial of blowing of trumpets.
precepts.point: Gideon divides the three hundred into three companies, a hundred to the left flank, a hundred down the middle, a hundred to the right, and puts a trumpet in every man's hand, with empty pitchers and lamps within the pitchers. Look on me, and do likewise: pay attention, and when I blow the trumpet, blow ye also on every side of the camp, and say, the sword of the Lord, and of Gideon.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

precepts.why:
Gideon “put a trumpet in every man’s hand” and told them, “When I blow with a trumpet, I and all that are with me, then blow ye the trumpets also on every side of all the camp.” That is the law of the trumpets in war: “And if ye go to war in your land against the enemy that oppresseth you, then ye shall blow an alarm with the trumpets; and ye shall be remembered before the Lord your God, and ye shall be saved from your enemies.”

Midian was the enemy that oppressed Israel in their own land, and the three hundred blew the alarm on every side of the camp, to be remembered before the Lord and saved. This is the history behind the shofars we blow. Those trumpets are not just for looks and thumbnails; there is a deep meaning behind them, going into the memorial of blowing of trumpets.
